# Multi-scale native-to-USD fixtures

These fixtures are generated by this repository's
[generate_units.py](../generate_units.py), not contributed assets or copied
Blender source. They are redistributable test data under the repository's
[license](../../../LICENSE). Blender is a separate generation and verification
process; the CTest consumes committed files without requiring Blender.

## Provenance

Generated and verified on Windows on 2026-10-04 with Blender 4.5.13 LTS
(`daeeeca98fb0`) and 5.2.2 LTS (`d13f752e3b9c`). All eight files are
uncompressed normal-save files with an active Scene. File-browser directories
are normalized to `//`; generator regressions exclude the user's home path.

## Cases

| Case | Nominal source scale | Source cube width | Presentation system |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unit-1m` | 1 | 1 | NONE |
| `unit-1cm` | 0.01 | 100 | METRIC |
| `unit-1mm` | 0.001 | 1000 | IMPERIAL |
| `unit-10m` | 10 | 0.1 | METRIC |

The selected `Units` Scene contains 16 Objects and one shared `UnitCube` Mesh.
An unselected Scene has scale 7, so normalization cannot come from an arbitrary
Scene. Four Objects use the eight-point, six-quad cube:

- `Cube` is an untransformed root at `/Asset/geo/Cube/mesh`.
- `Translated` has equivalent physical translation `(2, -3, 4)` in Blender's
  basis, represented by different saved source channels at each scale.
- `Parent` has translation, rotation and nonuniform negative scale.
- `mesh`, parented to `Parent`, adds translation, delta translation, rotation,
  nonuniform negative scale and a sheared/translated parent inverse.

Saved bit 2 of `Object.transflag` is 4 for the negative-world-handedness
`Parent` and its Empty children `mesh.1` and `mesh_1`, but zero for the doubly
reflected Mesh child `mesh`. Native transforms come from signed channels, not
from applying this cached flag again. Four-layout synthetic tests also prove
the flag cannot override the channels, and all other non-instance bits remain
fatal unsupported transforms.

Names exercise punctuation collisions (`A B`, `A/B`, `A_B`), natural suffixes,
`Cube.001` versus `Cube_001`, leading digits, Japanese fallback names and a
literal `Object` name. Children named `mesh`, `mesh.1` and `mesh_1` reserve the
Mesh parent's fixed data child. Five UV maps include `A/B` versus `A_B`, a
non-render `st`, active `Render Map`, and a Japanese fallback name.

## Oracle and checks

The generator reuses the integrated Scene oracle writer and comparator.
Adjacent UTF-8 `*.oracle.txt` files start with `BLEND_SCENE_ORACLE 1`:
saved scale and counts; Object parent/Mesh/render references and source
world/local matrices; Mesh points, topology, corner normals and per-corner
UV coordinates. `UNIT_SYSTEM` records the presentation label.
Four `WORLD_MESH` records add Blender-computed world-space vertices, independently
of native matrix construction. No evaluated modifier geometry is used.

Generation checks the oracle again after reopening the saved file.
`--check` regenerates only into temporary storage, compares semantic oracles,
then checks the stored file without rewriting it. Saved addresses and UI state
are not byte-reproducible. Matrices, points and normals use
`math.isclose(rel_tol=2e-6, abs_tol=2e-6)`; UV coordinates are exact, including
zero signs, as are names, references, flags, counts and topology.
[test_generate_units.py](../test_generate_units.py) covers
different-process/path reproduction, non-destructive success and failure,
home-path exclusion, changed-oracle rejection, and saved unit, transform,
geometry, name and UV mutations. The existing integrated Scene generator
regressions also exercise the shared writer.

`usdBlend.units` in
[AuthorSceneTests.cpp](../../../plugins/usdBlendFileFormat/tests/AuthorSceneTests.cpp)
decodes each unchanged file through native selection and Mesh decoding, then
authors and opens a USD layer. An independent `(x,z,-y)` and translation-only
unit mapping checks native and USD world/local matrices against Blender.
It checks all world vertices and their dimensions, points, topology, unscaled
normals and UVs, extent, `metersPerUnit = 1`, and Y-up. Direct cross-scale and
cross-version comparisons require matching points, world/local transforms,
world vertices, hierarchy, schemas and child order.

Matrix, world-vertex and Blender-derived dimension comparisons use
`2e-5 * (1 + abs(expected))`. Centered meter-space point magnitudes must be
within `1e-7` of `0.5`; USD extents, cross-scale points and the untransformed
and translated cubes' one-meter world dimensions use
`1e-7 * (1 + abs(expected))`. Blender's single-precision transformed vertices
are not held to the latter threshold: for example, the 4.5.13 `unit-10m`
translated source cube has normalized Y/Z bounds width `1.000000238418579`.
Native and USD geometry still satisfy the tighter one-meter check.

Exact ASCII identifiers, raw UTF-8 provenance, display names, collision suffixes,
fixed `mesh` and render `st` reservations and unsigned source-byte child ordering
are asserted against explicit expected names. Repeated and reversed native
block reads must author identical text for each input.

Commands are in the
[build guide](../../../docs/guides/building.md#multi-scale-unit-and-naming-oracles).
This evidence freezes [STAGE-O1](../../../docs/design/STAGE_CONTRACT.md#181-resolved-decisions)
and [NAME-O1](../../../docs/design/NAMING_POLICY.md#71-resolved-decisions);
it does not connect the importer, choose production input/traversal budgets,
or establish camera/light optical-unit mappings.
